newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat seeding stalls, corn harvest 8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat seeding stalls, corn harvest 8 pct.

text.p: Seedbed preparation and planting in Oklahoma wheat fields lagged a week behind the five year average due to heavy rains in the week ended Sunday, the state agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
Wheat was one percent seeded versus 8 last year and 6 six on average. Only 51 percent of seedbeds were prepared against 66 last year and 69 on average.
Heavy rains and cool temperatures in southern Oklahoma slowed fieldwork and crop development, but northern areas of the state still need more rain, it said.
Corn harvested eight percent vs 4 year ago, 15 average.
Corn mature 26 percent vs 51 y/a, 66 avge.
Corn rated 91 percent good to excellent, 7 fair, 2 poor.
Sorghum harvested 3 percent vs nil y/a, nil avge.
Sorghum mature 21 percent vs 6 y/a, 8 avge.
Sorghum rated 92 percent good to excellent, 6 fair.
Soybeans harvested 4 percent vs 2 y/a, one avge.
Soybeans mature 24 pct vs 15 y/a, 14 avge.
Soybeans rated 73 percent good to excellent, 20 fair.
Cotton bolls opening 8 percent vs 2 y/a, 7 avge.
Cotton rated 58 percent good to excellent, 22 fair.
Pasture and range condition was rated 83 percent good to excellent, versus 68 percent at that level last week.
